decisions.reason: The quoted sentence directly states that CLN3 Batten disease 'manifests as vision loss early in life', which directly supports the has_phenotype relationship. Vision loss is a clinical phenotype clearly attributed to the disease.

The quoted sentence explicitly states that CLN3 Batten disease 'progresses to neurological dysfunction', which directly supports the has_phenotype relationship. Neurological dysfunction is a clinical phenotype clearly attributed to the disease.

The quoted sentence directly states that a splice-switching ASO 'can reduce neurological disease burden in mouse models of CLN3 disease', which demonstrates a therapeutic effect on the disease. The evidence clearly establishes that this treatment approach reduces disease burden.

The quoted sentence states ASO treatment 'resulted in higher amplitudes on electroretinograms, suggesting mitigation of retinal dysfunction'. While the quote uses 'suggesting' rather than directly stating mitigation, the context establishes that improved electroretinogram amplitudes indicate reduction of retinal dysfunction, supporting a therapeutic effect. The abstract clearly links this treatment to amelioration of retinal phenotype.
